name: Avaza
description: Avaza is a work-management platform for projects, tasks, resource scheduling, time and expenses, quotes, invoices and team collaboration. Professional-services teams use it to plan client delivery, coordinate people and track operational and financial work in one account.
agentUseSummary: Relay uses a dedicated customer-admin-generated Avaza personal access token with only read_projects, binds the connection to one preselected project ID, and exposes one metadata-only project-state read. Titles, notes, companies, sections, members, rates, budgets, tags, other resources, writes and arbitrary API, webhook or MCP access remain blocked.

capabilities.label: Read selected project state
capabilities.description: Read one selected project's ID, status flags and lifecycle dates.

allowed.label: Read selected project state
allowed.description: Use the fixed individual-project route for one selected project and return only bounded lifecycle metadata.

blocked.label: Expose private project data
blocked.description: Titles, codes, notes, companies, owners, sections, members, emails, rates, budgets, tags, URLs, categories, billing configuration and identities are excluded.

blocked.label: Read broader Avaza resources
blocked.description: Project lists, other projects, contacts, companies, users, tasks, schedules, timesheets, expenses, invoices, estimates, bills, payments, webhooks and account configuration are blocked.

blocked.label: Mutate Avaza
blocked.description: Projects, members, tasks, schedules, time, expenses, financials, files, webhooks, configuration and every write or destructive action are blocked.

blocked.label: Run arbitrary Avaza calls
blocked.description: Agents cannot choose origins, paths, IDs, fields, filters, searches, pagination, bodies, scopes or raw REST, webhook or MCP operations.

approvalProfiles.label: Selected Project State Read
approvalProfiles.description: Read one selected project's bounded lifecycle state; private content, people, companies, financials, other resources, administration and mutations remain blocked.

runtimeSupport.description: Mount one no-input selected-project state reader backed by Railway's fixed-origin Avaza adapter and an encrypted read_projects personal access token.
Mount one no-input selected-project state reader backed by Railway's fixed-origin Avaza adapter and an encrypted read_projects personal access token.

providerSetup.blocker: Avaza personal access tokens are created by an account Administrator and inherit both selected scopes and the creating user's account permissions. No paid disposable account, synthetic project or dedicated admin-owned token was available in this lane, and provider-console work is separately owned.
providerSetup.nextAction: In the provider-console acceptance task, use a paid disposable Avaza account containing only synthetic data, create a dedicated admin-owned personal access token with exactly read_projects, bind one synthetic project ID through Relay, then validate metadata-only output, other-project and broader-resource denial, rate handling, token deletion, disconnect and post-disconnect denial. Never reuse a production administrator token or grant write_projects.

evidence.supports: Avaza's official public Swagger reference documents the fixed HTTPS API origin, GET /api/Project/{id}, exact read_projects scope, PascalCase project response fields and broad adjacent private read/write resources.

Avaza's official authentication guidance documents administrator-created personal access tokens, creator permission inheritance, granular access scopes, one-time token display, Bearer authentication and token deletion.
Avaza's official OAuth guidance documents granular comma-separated scopes, fixed authorization and token endpoints, access and refresh lifetimes and the broader alternative authorization-code flow.
Avaza's official webhook guide documents project and other account events plus webhook creation, confirming an adjacent stateful surface excluded from this connector.
Avaza's current terms establish subscription and user authority, access levels, API-call limits, customer-data responsibilities and third-party application obligations.
Avaza's current privacy policy describes account and service data handled by the platform, reinforcing exclusion of private project, people and company data.
